slides.title: What is Posture?
slides.english_text:
What is Posture?
• Posture a composite of the positions of all the joints of the body at any given moment
• Ideal posture an alignment of maximum physiological and biomechanical efficiency, which requires a minimum of stress and strain
• Faulty posture the posture that is not an ideal posture
(Muscles Testing and function, Kendall et
al, 1952)

slides.title: Spastic diplegia
slides.english_text:
Spastic diplegia
A common manifestation of cerebral
palsy. It primarily affects the legs,
although there may be considerable
asymmetry between the two sides.
The commonest pattern consists of
o Hip flexion and internal rotation,
due to overactivity by the ilipsoas,
rectus femoris and hip adductors.
o Knee flexion, due to overactivity of
the hamstrings, especially on the
medial side
o Equines deformity of the foot and
eversion of the hindfoot, due to
overactivity by the triceps surae and
peronei.

slides.title: Shuffling gait
slides.english_text:
Shuffling gait
Parkinsonism
The commonest pattern consists of
• Stride length and speed were very much reduces, although cycle time was usually normal
• The walking base was slightly increased
• The range of motion at the hip, knee and ankle were all decreased, mainly by a reduction in joint extension
• The swinging of the arms was much reduced
• The majority of patients rotated the trunk in phase with the pelvis instead of twisting it in the opposite direction
• The vertical trajectories of the head, heel and toe were all reduced although other workers have commented on a distinct ‘bobbing’ motion of the head.

slides.title: Trendelenburg Gait
slides.english_text:
Trendelenburg Gait
The Trendelenburg gait occurs due to
weakness of the hip abductor muscles
(gluteus medius), primarily on the stance
leg. This weakness prevents stabilization of
the pelvis during walking.
The commonest pattern consists of
• Contralateral Pelvic Drop: During the • stance phase of the affected leg, the pelvis drops on the opposite (swing) side.
• Lateral Trunk Lean (Compensation): • The patient leans their trunk laterally over the affected stance leg to shift their center of gravity and reduce the demand on weak abductors.

Cat.
Stage
Definition
類別
階段
定義
I
Lyer
Unable to walk / unable to sit without support>1min / assist to sit
躺臥者
無法行走 / 無法在沒有支持的情況下坐超過 1 分鐘 / 協助坐下
II
Sitter
Sit without support >1min / unable to walk with 1 person assistance

weight)

Assisted Walker

Supervised

Outdoor Walker
Walk independently on level or non-level surfaces
戶外步行者
